cards.title: Automated Monitoring of Institute Closure Risk (Account Management Stage)
cards.body:
Automated Monitoring of Institute Closure Risk (Account Management Stage)


Field
Description / Instruction
Problem Statement
Institutes onboarded under NBFC partnerships carry asymmetric risk: sudden closures or operational disruptions can severely impact loan portfolio health. Currently, there is no systematic monitoring mechanism post-onboarding. We need to implement a recurring, automated process that pulls risk signals from public sources and flags potential early warnings for ALL institutes during account management stage.
Sizing of Problem / Expected Business Impact
- Portfolio exposure = all active partner institutes. - Early detection can prevent ₹-crore scale risk events by pre-emptively stopping disbursals, reallocating exposure, or renegotiating partnerships. - Impact: risk mitigation, stronger BD decisions, compliance readiness, improved investor confidence.
Personas Impacted
Internal: Risk & Compliance team, BD, Product, Analytics, Account Management, Ops. External: Partner institutes, Regulators.
Dependencies
- Access to public APIs/portals: GST portal, MCA database, EPFO, LinkedIn. - Scraping/sentiment APIs for Google/Twitter/Reddit reviews. - Infra for automation (ETL pipeline, scheduler). - Alignment with BD/Risk on alert thresholds. - Legal/compliance check for scraping/automation.
Proposed Output
- Automated Report (Monthly/Quarterly): Flags institutes with anomalies in GST, MCA, EPFO, employee counts, or negative sentiment. - Dashboard: Portfolio-wide heat map of risk levels (Green/Amber/Red). - SOP Document: Defines monitoring cadence, ownership (Risk/BD), alert thresholds, and escalation steps. - Integration Plan: Alerts flow into CRM/BD pipeline for action.
Classification Tag
Tech Card(only if required) + BAU/MIS (recurring monitoring).
Priority
High – Core NBFC risk management; should run on regular intervals (e.g., monthly) across all institutes.
Tentative Solution Framework
Data Ingestion (Automated at Regular Intervals)
GST filing regularity → scrape/portal check.
MCA annual returns & financials → API pull.
EPFO filings → employee contribution & count trends.
LinkedIn company pages → employee count changes/posts etc
Google/Twitter/Reddit/LinkedIn → sentiment analysis of reviews & mentions.
Processing & Thresholds
Example thresholds:
GST/MCA: Missing ≥2 filings = Amber; ≥3 = Red.
EPFO: ≥10% employee drop vs last quarter = Amber; ≥20% = Red.
LinkedIn: sudden headcount drop = Red.
Sentiment: >30% negative reviews in last 3 months = Amber; >50% = Red.
Dashboard & Reports
Portfolio-wide heat map of institutes.
Auto-emailed monthly report to Risk + BD.
SOP & Escalation Path
Green = No action.
Amber = BD team follow-up call with institute.
Red = Risk committee review; potential freeze on further exposure.







Check public sources: 
Of growth: GST returns regularity, MCA returns regularity, MCA financials analysis, EPFO filing - amount and employee count, LinkedIn Employee count. Some of this feeds back to BD. Automate most of these things, so that reports come
Online review scraping: Google, Twitter, LinkedIn, Reddit. Automate this.

Opportunity: conversational lead capture can increase lead volume/quality vs static landing experiences (supported by recent large-scale field experiments in conversational vs landing approaches).
Business impact target: improve conversion from landing → TOFU (by page + by vertical), and downstream outcomes (qualified → connected → conversion).

External
Website visitors (prospects at admission stage, loan stage, post-loan stage)
Internal
Marketing / Growth
Admissions team (CF)
Loan team (PSE/ELC)
Disbursement / Forex / Cross-sell teams
Product, Tech, Analytics, Leadership
Dependencies
Bot content library & policy (approved answers only; guardrails to avoid hallucinations / mis-selling).
Consent + privacy flows for phone capture and processing personal data (DPDP; plus RBI digital lending requirements if bot participates in digital lending acquisition).
Lead routing + attribution to the right vertical (Admission vs Loan vs Cross-sell)
CRM ingestion + dedupe + user-level mapping (no duplicate records)
Event tracking + experimentation platform (A/B)
Proposed Output
Strategic Review → “AI Bot MVP Spec” (before Tech Card)
A) Bot Scope (What it should do)
Identify intent (within 1–2 questions)
Admission TOFU (Consultant Finder / counselling)
Loan TOFU (loan eligibility / connect to PSE/ELC)
Post-loan cross-sell (disbursement/forex/support)
Guide + qualify with minimal friction
Use quick-replies/playbooks (qualify + route), similar to standard conversational playbooks approach.
Capture phone number (minimum) with explicit consent
Phone first, then optional email / key qualifiers (country/intake/admit status/loan amount etc.)
Route to correct TOFU pipeline
Admission lead → admissions pipeline
Loan lead → loan pipeline
Cross-sell → relevant team queue
Safe fallback + handoff
If question is out-of-scope or high-risk → show curated options / connect to human
B) Non-Goals (Explicit)
Not replacing the website forms entirely
Not promising loan approval/sanction, rates, timelines
Not giving personalized financial advice
Not enabling unbounded Q&A without guardrails
C) Measurement Plan (Throughput-first)
Primary metric (must):
Landing → TOFU conversion rate by page and by vertical
Secondary funnel metrics:
Landing → bot opened
Bot opened → intent classified
Intent classified → phone captured
Phone captured → qualified (basic fields)
Qualified → connected (call/WA)
Connected → conversion (vertical-specific KPI)
Incrementality methodology:
A/B test: same pages, control (no bot) vs variant (bot), measure lift in landing→TOFU and downstream.
D) Placement Strategy (to avoid cannibalization noise)
Start with top traffic / high-intent pages where drop-offs are high:
loan eligibility pages, course/country pages, consultant pages, FAQ-heavy pages
Gradual rollout by page clusters
E) Compliance & Risk Controls
Clear consent notice before phone capture (purpose + usage)
Data minimization: capture only what’s needed at each stage (DPDP).
If used for digital lending acquisition, ensure alignment with RBI digital lending directions on disclosures/data/privacy controls.
Content guardrails: bot answers from approved sources only.
Classification Tag
Strategic Review (Output = AI Bot MVP Spec + Experiment Plan + “Ready Tech Card”)
Priority
High
Milestones
Discovery Spike
Page shortlist + intent taxonomy (Admission / Loan / Cross-sell)
Conversation flows (playbooks)
Content library draft + approvals
Measurement + A/B design
Compliance review checklist
MVP Pilot
Bot on selected pages (10–20% traffic)
A/B test readout (2–4 weeks)
Scale Decision
If lift achieved → convert to Tech Card for full rollout + integrations
Success Metrics
+X% lift in Landing → TOFU conversion per vertical (primary)
Improved lead quality: connect rate / downstream conversion
Reduced time-to-resolution for common FAQs (engagement quality)
Notes for Grooming
“Bot lead count” is not the goal; page landing throughput is the goal.
Guardrails + consent + attribution must be designed before any production launch.

cards.title: One-Time Scholarship Data Extraction for SEO Seeding

Analytics Card:
1. Problem
Acme is launching a Scholarships SEO vertical but currently lacks a structured, high-coverage scholarship dataset to power:
SEO landing pages (country, degree, field, provider, deadlines)
Scholarship detail pages
Internal discovery and recommendation flows
The absence of a clean base dataset blocks:
Page generation at scale
Content standardization
SEO indexing velocity
Current PRD expects structured scholarship coverage across multiple dimensions (country, degree, field, provider, eligibility, funding type, deadlines), but no centralized dataset exists to support this.
Ref: Acme_Scholarships_Product_SEO_PRD.docx
2. Goals
Build a high-quality, structured scholarship master dataset via one-time web extraction
Enable fast SEO page generation across all target dimensions
Ensure data completeness + usability for content and product teams
3. User Stories
As a content/person16@example.com, I want a structured dataset so I can generate SEO pages at scale
As a product team, I want normalized scholarship attributes to build filters and discovery
As a user, I want accurate scholarship info (deadline, eligibility, amount)
4. Scope
In Scope
One-time extraction of scholarships from internet sources
Schema design for scholarship dataset (SEO-aligned)
Deduplication + normalization of records
Enrichment for missing key attributes where possible
Output: clean dataset usable for SEO + product
Out of Scope
Automated scraping pipeline
Real-time updates / refresh logic
Continuous monitoring of deadlines
Full data verification across all records
5. Data Schema (Proposed Output Fields)
Aligned with SEO PRD requirements:
Core Identity
scholarship_id (generated)
scholarship_name
provider_name
provider_type (govt / university / private / foundation)
Coverage Dimensions (for SEO pages)
country

degree_level (UG / PG / PhD / MBA etc.)
field_of_study (standardized taxonomy)
Eligibility & Targeting

min_academic_requirement
test_requirements (IELTS/GRE/etc.)
Financials

scholarship_amount
currency

application_deadline

Links & Source
application_url
source_url
last_verified_at (timestamp)
SEO/Content Enhancers
description (cleaned)
tags (derived: merit-based, need-based, women-only etc.)
popularity_signal (if available or derived)

Since sources are undefined, extraction should cover:
Tier 1 (High trust)
Govt scholarship portals
Official university scholarship pages
Tier 2
Scholarship aggregators
Study abroad blogs
Tier 3
Forums / community sites (low priority, high noise)
Approach:
Start broad → filter → deduplicate → prioritize high-confidence records
7. Methodology
Source Discovery

Extract from top N SERP results across key keywords:
“scholarships for Indian students abroad”
“fully funded scholarships USA/UK/Canada”
Data Extraction
Semi-automated scraping + manual QA layer
Capture structured + unstructured fields
Normalization
Standardize:
countries
degree levels
funding types
fields of study

Rule-based matching:
scholarship_name + provider + country
Enrichment
Fill missing attributes where possible
Tag classification for SEO use

M3: Cleaning + normalization (3–4 days)
M4: Final dataset + QA + handoff (2–3 days)

Total unique scholarships extracted

Coverage:
countries
degree levels
funding types
% records with valid application URLs

country
degree level
funding type

All major SEO page types defined in PRD

Tag: data-infra
Assigned to: Person 17
Business Owner: [Needs assignment]

---

Current State

The university and course pages on Acme.com display data that was last refreshed at an unknown date — likely stale. This includes university names, course details, fees, rankings, and other metadata. Stale data hurts SEO rankings (Google rewards fresh, accurate content) and limits the number of pages we can publish (no data = no page).

Quantified pain:
- SEO ranking decay on existing university/course pages due to outdated information
- Inability to launch new pages for universities/courses not yet in our database — each new page is a potential lead generation asset
- Student trust erosion when displayed data doesn't match current reality

Target State

- A refreshed, accurate dataset of university and course information scraped from authoritative sources
- Data structured for direct ingestion into the Acme CMS/database
- Enough new data to enable launch of additional university/course pages
- Automated or semi-automated pipeline that can be re-run periodically (quarterly or semesterly)

Technical Approach

1. Identify sources: University websites, ranking aggregators, government databases, course listing platforms
2. Build scraping pipeline: Python (Scrapy/BeautifulSoup/Playwright) scripts to extract: university name, country, ranking, courses offered, tuition fees, intake dates, eligibility criteria, application deadlines
3. Data cleaning and deduplication: Standardize university and course names, handle currency conversions, remove duplicates
4. Validation: Cross-reference scraped data with existing Acme database. Flag discrepancies for manual review
5. Load: Import cleaned data into Acme database/CMS

Risks & Rollback

- Anti-scraping blocks (Cloudflare, CAPTCHAs): High likelihood, medium impact. Mitigation: rotating proxies, respectful rate limiting, headless browser.
- Data accuracy — scraped data is wrong: Medium likelihood, high impact. Mitigation: cross-reference multiple sources, manual QA on top 50 universities.
- Schema mismatch with Acme DB: Low likelihood. Mitigation: map fields before scraping, align with existing schema.
- Rollback: If scraped data is bad, existing data remains untouched — the scrape populates a staging table, not production.

Testing & Validation

- Scrape a pilot batch of 50 universities across 3 countries
- Manual verification of accuracy for the pilot batch (spot-check 20%)
- Confirm data loads correctly into staging environment
- Verify page rendering with new data before production push

Timeline & Phases

Phase 1: Identify sources, build scraping scripts for top 5 countries (Week 1-2)
Phase 2: Run full scrape, clean data, load to staging (Week 3)
Phase 3: QA + production push + launch new pages (Week 4)

We have a large pool of historical leads (3 months) that are currently stagnant. We need to automate a re-engagement engine that uses cost-effective IVR (140-series) to filter for "Active Intent" and only spends WhatsApp API costs on users who explicitly ask for a link by pressing "1".
2. Automation Logic (The "Schedule")
A. Weekday "Fresh Lead" Run (Mon–Thu)
Time: 10:00 AM daily.
Query Filter: created_at = Yesterday.
Volume: Low/Moderate.
Action: Trigger IVR → If DTMF 1 → Send WhatsApp ID 8540812.
B. Weekend "Deep Burn" Run (Fri, Sat, Sun)
Time: 10:00 AM daily.
Query Filter: created_at = Last 3 Months.
Deduplication Rule: Exclude any user who has been called by this specific automation in the last 30 days. (Critical to prevent harassment).
Action: Trigger IVR (140-series) → If DTMF 1 → Send WhatsApp ID 8540812.
3. Technical Workflow
Source: Metabase Query 668.
Transport: Automated CSV push or API POST to TataTele.
IVR Config: Use 140-series outbound caller ID. Script must end with "Press 1 to receive your loan eligibility link on WhatsApp."
Real-time Trigger: TataTele webhook sends "Success + Input:1" to our middleware (Interakt/HubSpot).
Destination: WhatsApp message sent immediately upon trigger.
4. Acceptance Criteria
AC 1: Users from 90 days ago MUST be included in the Saturday/Sunday runs.
AC 2: A user who was called last Saturday MUST NOT be called again this Sunday (cooldown period of 30 days).
AC 3: WhatsApp must only trigger on DTMF "1". No message should be sent for "No Input," "Hanging up," or other digits.
AC 4: If the Metabase query returns 0 leads (e.g., error), the system must retry 3 times at 30-minute intervals.
5. Rollback & Monitoring
Monitoring: Track IVR_Calls_Placed vs WA_Links_Sent. If the ratio is < 1%, alert the Business Owner (indicates potential IVR audio issue or low-quality old leads).
Safety Valve: Ability to manually pause the weekend "Deep Burn" without stopping the "Weekday Fresh" runs.
Failure Detection: Alert Slack if the TataTele webhook fails to reach our WhatsApp trigger system for > 5 consecutive intents.

cards.body:
PRD: LE Logic Update – Gram Panchayat Property Eligibility (Canara Bank)

BACKGROUND
Acme's current LE logic blanket-rejects all applications where collateral is Gram Panchayat property (except Kerala). Two Canara Bank cases were incorrectly closed as not eligible by Acme's ELC team. Both applicants later got Canara Bank loans approved directly using the same panchayat-based collateral. Canara Bank does accept Gram Panchayat properties if specific criteria are met.

Source: Email thread "Clarification Required on Panchayat Property as Collateral – Canara Bank Cases" (April 15–16, 2026) – Pratik Garg (Sales Head), Ravi Sharma, Person 19 Singh, Durga Vinay Simhadri

OBJECTIVE
1. Update the LE Form to include questions assessing Gram Panchayat collateral suitability — collected at the collateral step, before LE logic runs
2. Update LE logic to conditionally pass/fail instead of blanket rejection
3. Mandate ELC agents to fill collateral details in GD CRM before triggering LE

STAKEHOLDERS
- Requester: Pratik Garg (Sales Head)
- Business Owner: Ravi Sharma
- VP – Partnerships: Person 19 Singh
- Product: Person 14
- ELC / Ops: Internal Team

CURRENT BEHAVIOR (AS-IS)
LE rule: if collateral_type == Gram Panchayat AND state != Kerala → REJECT
No further property assessment questions are asked.
ELC agents skip CRM collateral updates when they assume a case will be rejected.

DESIRED BEHAVIOR (TO-BE)
For Gram Panchayat collateral: surface qualifying questions inline at the collateral step, before LE logic runs. Canara Bank then appears in results normally if eligible.

UX APPROACH
These questions are NOT added to the global LE form. They appear only as a conditional extension of the collateral step, triggered when the user selects "Gram Panchayat" as their collateral type.

Why collateral step is the right placement:
- User is already thinking about their property — questions feel natural, not bank-specific
- LE logic needs the answers before it runs, so Canara Bank appears (or doesn't) in results like any other bank — no special UI or post-results CTAs needed
- Zero friction for users with any other collateral type

Flow:
User fills LE form
→ Selects collateral type
→ If "Gram Panchayat": additional property questions appear inline (same step)
→ If anything else: no change, LE runs as before
→ LE logic runs with complete data
→ Results shown — Canara Bank appears if eligible, just like any other bank

NEW QUESTIONS FOR LE FORM (shown only when collateral = Gram Panchayat)

Q1. Is the property classified as Non-Agricultural under Section 142?
Input: Yes / No

Q2. Is the property approved by the Zilla Parishad?
Input: Yes / No

Q3. Are the Gram Panchayat taxes paid and up to date?
Input: Yes / No

Q4. What type of property is it?
Input: Dropdown → [Constructed / Open Plot]

→ If Constructed:
Q4a. Is the layout map approved by the Gram Panchayat or Zilla Parishad?
Input: Yes / No

→ If Open Plot:
Q4b. What is the boundary status of the plot?
Input: Dropdown → [Plot has boundary above 4ft / Plot does not have boundary above 4ft]

Q5. Does the property have four-wheeler access?
Input: Yes / No

Total questions: Max 5 (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q4a or Q4b, Q5) — always conditional, never all shown at once.

UPDATED LE LOGIC (PROPOSED)
IF collateral = Gram Panchayat:
Q1 + Q2 + Q3 must all be YES (mandatory gates)
Q5 must be YES (mandatory gate)

IF Q4 = Constructed:
Q4a must be YES → ELIGIBLE for Canara Bank
Q4a = NO → NOT ELIGIBLE for Canara Bank

IF Q4 = Open Plot:
Q4b = "Plot has boundary above 4ft" → ELIGIBLE for Canara Bank
Q4b = "Plot does not have boundary above 4ft" → NOT ELIGIBLE for Canara Bank

If any mandatory gate (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q5) fails → NOT ELIGIBLE for Canara Bank

SCOPE OF WORK
Product: Finalize question wording, document LE logic rules, create test cases for all branches (constructed pass/fail, open plot pass/fail, mandatory gate failures)
Engineering: Add conditional question flow in LE Form triggered on Gram Panchayat collateral selection; dropdown for Q4; conditional sub-question (Q4a or Q4b) based on Q4 selection; update LE decision logic for Canara Bank; make CRM collateral fields mandatory before LE trigger
ELC/Ops: Train team to fill CRM collateral fields regardless of assumed outcome; add to LE Tracker

OUT OF SCOPE (v1)
- Other lenders (Canara Bank only)
- State-level geographic overrides beyond existing Kerala exception
- Automated CRM validation enforcement

SUCCESS METRICS
- Reduction in incorrect Gram Panchayat rejections for Canara Bank: ≥ 90%
- LE completion rate for Canara Bank + Gram Panchayat cases: track pre vs. post
- CRM collateral field fill rate by ELC: 100%

RISKS & ASSUMPTIONS
- Assumption: Canara Bank's Gram Panchayat policy is consistent across branches (confirm with Pratik Garg)
- Risk: Without mandatory CRM fields in system, ELC agents may continue skipping them
- Risk: Other lenders may have different Gram Panchayat policies — keep scope tight

PRE-REQUISITE TO VALIDATE
Is collateral type currently collected in the LE form before results are shown? If not, this requires a broader form redesign discussion before implementation can begin.

Created from: Email thread, April 2026 | Raised by: Pratik Garg | PRD by: Person 14

Product Requirements Document

AI Collections Bot — Loan Bounce Recovery

Acme | Collections Team
Version: 1.7 | Date: May 2026 | Status: Draft for Review

1. Problem Statement

Acme's collections team manually handles 700–800 EMI bounce cases every month. 60% of these resolve between the 5th and 12th of each month — the "Golden Window" — aligned with typical salary credit cycles, through standard payment reminders. However, manual agents spend the bulk of their time on repetitive reminder calls and failed attempts (RNR), leaving little capacity for nuanced negotiations on older, harder buckets.

As the portfolio scales, this model breaks down. At 1,500+ cases/month, the team would need to hire 4–5 additional agents just to maintain current throughput — and the Golden Window would still be under-served because of the ramp-up time and coordination overhead manual processes require.

A Pilot conducted with Predixion AI validated the opportunity: across 450 cases, the bot recovered payment from 130 customers (29%) within 2 days, with a live payment link flow and no human involvement for standard cases.

2. Goals & Success Metrics


3. Scope

In Scope

Automated outbound calling for EMI bounce cases where Lender == "Acme"
Payment link delivery via WhatsApp with SMS fallback
Scheduled WhatsApp payment link reminders (30 minutes before customer's stated payment time)
SIP-based transfer to Tata Tele human agents
Callback scheduling: capturing preferred time/date from the customer and enforcing a suppression window in the CRM
Disposition and call recording write-back to the Acme CRM
Compliance guardrails (call frequency, call window enforcement)
Monitoring, alerting, and a Kill Switch

Out of Scope

Bounce cases for third-party lenders
Inbound call handling
Legal/legal-escalation flows
WhatsApp conversations beyond payment link delivery

4. Target Users

Collections Manager — monitors bot performance, reviews call recordings for tone and compliance, manages escalations
Collections Agents / ELCs — receive callback tasks from the bot for complex or disputed cases
Tech/Ops — manages CRM triggers, API health, and system configuration

5. System Architecture & Flow

5.0 Bot Persona


Open Question #11 (see Section 17): How does the bot detect which language to open the call in — customer's registered state, prior interaction history, or a fixed default?

5.1 Trigger

The Acme CRM identifies leads where Loan_Status == "EMI_BOUNCE" AND Lender == "Acme" and pushes the lead to Ringg AI via API. Leads triggered between the 5th and 12th of the month (the Golden Window) are given scheduling priority.

5.2 Visual Flow Diagram

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Acme CRM │
│ Loan_Status = EMI_BOUNCE AND Lender = Acme │
│ Check: attempt_count_today < 3 AND callback_scheduled_at clear │
└───────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
│ API Push (Lead Payload)
▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Ringg AI Bot (Somya) │
│ Call Window: 10 AM – 7 PM │ Max 3 attempts/day │
│ │
│ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────┐ │
│ │ Path A │ │ Path B/C │ │ Path E │ │
│ │ Pay Now │ │ Callback / │ │ Human Requested │ │
│ │ │ │ Can't Pay │ │ │ │
│ └──────┬──────┘ └──────┬──────┘ └──────────┬───────────┘ │
│ │ │ │ │
│ ▼ ▼ ▼ │
│ Send Payment Link Schedule callback Book ELC Queue Slot │
│ (WhatsApp → SMS) in CRM in CRM │
│ OR schedule WA │
│ reminder -30 mins │
└─────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│ │
│ [If SIP confirmed — ON HOLD] │
▼ ▼
┌──────────────┐ ┌───────────────────────┐
│ Tata Tele │ │ ELC Agent Queue │
│ Human Agent │ │ (Manual Callback) │
│ SIP Bridge │ └───────────┬───────────┘
└──────────────┘ │
│
┌───────────────────────────────────────────┘
│ Post-Call Write-back (All Paths)
▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Acme CRM │
│ Write: disposition, call_duration, recording_url, │
│ payment_link_sent, callback_scheduled_at, │
│ payment_intent_time, whatsapp_reminder_scheduled_at, │
│ attempt_count_today + 1 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

5.3 Data Pushed to Bot (Lead Payload)


5.4 Bot Execution Logic

Call Window: 08:00 AM – 7:00 PM only. Leads triggered outside this window are queued for the next available slot.

Attempt Cap: Maximum 3 call attempts per lead per day. The CRM enforces this before firing the API request to Ringg AI. Ringg AI performs a secondary check using attempt_count_today in the payload as a safety net. Any trigger received at count ≥ 3 is rejected at the CRM layer and logged as DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

Callback Suppression: Before placing any call, the CRM checks callback_scheduled_at. If set and within 48 hours in the future, the lead is suppressed and no API call is made to Ringg AI.

Conversation Flow:

Bot introduces itself as Somya from Acme and states the bounce reason and amount
Bot offers to send a payment link immediately
If customer says yes → send payment link via WhatsApp (SMS fallback within 120s if delivery fails)
If customer says no to immediate link → bot asks for preferred payment time; schedules WhatsApp payment link 30 minutes before payment_intent_time; bot writes payment_intent_time to CRM; CRM checks payment status at payment_intent_time + 2 hours — if payment not received, CRM re-triggers a bot call
If the customer says they will pay later or asks to be called back → bot captures preferred date/time, confirms verbally, writes callback_scheduled_at to CRM (separate from payment_intent_time)
If the customer requests a human agent → see Section 5.5
If no answer or call drops mid-conversation → disposition logged as RNR or RNR_MID_CALL; retry scheduled within the same day up to the 3-attempt cap

5.5 Human Handoff ⚠️ ON HOLD (Pending Ringg AI SIP Confirmation)

We need to verify whether Ringg AI supports SIP transfer / direct interconnect before this flow can be built. AC-2 and AC-4 are blocked on this.

Interim Behaviour (active until SIP is confirmed):

When a customer says they want to talk to a human agent, the bot will:

Acknowledge gracefully — "Sure, let me get someone from our team to call you back."
Write callback_scheduled_at = next available ELC queue slot to the CRM
Suppress all further automated bot calls to that lead until the ELC callback is logged
Log disposition as HUMAN_REQUESTED

Queue Logic:

Next available slot is determined by CRM based on current ELC agent load
If no slot available within current call window, lead is queued for next business day at 10:00 AM
No further bot attempts are made until the ELC logs their disposition

5.6 Payment Link Flow

On customer request, the bot triggers a WhatsApp message with the payment link immediately. If the customer declines an immediate link but provides a preferred payment time, the system schedules a WhatsApp message with the payment link 30 minutes before payment_intent_time. In both cases, if WhatsApp delivery fails, an SMS with the same link is automatically sent within 120 seconds (AC-3).

payment_intent_time and callback_scheduled_at are separate fields with separate purposes and must not be conflated:


⚠️ Path A Exception — Architect Review Required:
In Path A (customer declines immediate link, provides preferred payment time), the bot call script currently writes callback_scheduled_at = payment_intent_time. This is functionally effective for suppressing bot calls until the payment window, but is architecturally inconsistent with the field separation principle above. Resolution needed before Sprint 1: either treat this as a documented exception, or update the script to write only payment_intent_time and let the CRM derive call suppression independently.

5.7 Post-Call Write-back Field Mapping

All fields are written by Ringg AI to the Acme CRM immediately after every call ends.


6. Ringg AI — API Integration Details

Note: Fields below are placeholders. Tech to populate with actual values from Ringg AI onboarding documentation before Sprint 1 begins.

6.1 Outbound Call Trigger (CRM → Ringg AI)


6.2 Post-Call Write-back (Ringg AI → CRM)


6.3 Scheduled WhatsApp Dispatch (Ringg AI → WhatsApp)


6.4 Kill Switch


7. Disposition Code Enumeration

Full list of valid values for the disposition_code field written back to the CRM after every call.


8. Acceptance Criteria

AC-1 — The 3-Call Guardrail (RBI Compliance)

GIVEN a lead has already been called 3 times today,
WHEN a new trigger is received from the CRM,
THEN the system must reject the call attempt, log the rejection, and return a DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED disposition — with zero calls placed.

AC-2 — The SIP Bridge (Audio Quality) ⚠️ ON HOLD

Blocked on Section 5.5. Will be scoped once Ringg AI confirms SIP interconnect support.

AC-3 — Payment Link Fallback

GIVEN a payment link needs to be sent (immediately or via scheduled reminder),
WHEN WhatsApp delivery fails,
THEN an SMS containing the same payment link must be automatically dispatched within 120 seconds, with no manual intervention required.

AC-4 — Agent Busy Failover ⚠️ ON HOLD

Blocked on Section 5.5. Will be scoped once Ringg AI confirms SIP interconnect support.

AC-5 — Callback Scheduling & Suppression

GIVEN a customer requests a callback during a bot call,
WHEN the bot captures the preferred date and time,
THEN the bot must (a) confirm the slot verbally, (b) write callback_scheduled_at to the CRM immediately after the call, and (c) suppress all further automated bot call attempts until that datetime has passed — provided it is within 48 hours.
If the requested callback time is more than 48 hours away, the CRM records the preference but standard retry logic continues unaffected.

AC-6 — Human Request → ELC Queue

GIVEN a customer requests a human agent during a bot call,
WHEN the bot detects this intent,
THEN the bot must (a) acknowledge gracefully, (b) write callback_scheduled_at as the next available ELC queue slot, (c) log disposition as HUMAN_REQUESTED, and (d) suppress all further bot call attempts until the ELC callback disposition is logged.

AC-7 — Scheduled WhatsApp Payment Reminder & 2-Hour Payment Check

GIVEN a customer declines an immediate payment link but provides a preferred payment time,
WHEN the bot captures payment_intent_time,
THEN the system must (a) write payment_intent_time and whatsapp_reminder_scheduled_at (payment_intent_time minus 30 minutes) to the CRM as separate fields from callback_scheduled_at, (b) dispatch the WhatsApp payment link at exactly whatsapp_reminder_scheduled_at with SMS fallback within 120 seconds if delivery fails, and (c) at payment_intent_time + 2 hours, check payment status — if payment has not been received, re-trigger a bot call to the lead.

9. Compliance & Constraints

Calling hours strictly enforced: 10:00 AM – 7:00 PM
Maximum 3 call attempts per lead per calendar day — enforced at CRM layer; Ringg AI secondary check via attempt_count_today
Callback suppression is system-enforced — no lead with an active callback_scheduled_at within 48 hours should receive a bot call
payment_intent_time and callback_scheduled_at are distinct fields — the CRM must not conflate them; the 2-hour payment check re-trigger is independent of callback suppression logic
Leads with HUMAN_REQUESTED disposition must not receive further bot calls until ELC callback is completed and logged
All bot scripts must be reviewed and approved by the Collections Manager before go-live
100% of call recordings must be retained and accessible via CRM for compliance audits

10. Structured Timeline & Milestones


11. Staging & Sandbox Environment Specification


12. UAT Parallel Run Plan & Sign-off Criteria

Parallel Run Structure

During Week 5, the bot and manual ELC agents will work the same bounce lead cohort simultaneously — bot handles outbound calls, ELC monitors outcomes in real time.


UAT Sign-off Criteria

All of the following must be met before go-live approval:


Sign-off requires written approval from the Collections Manager before production launch proceeds.

13. Monitoring & Reliability

Kill Switch: A "Global Stop" control in the CRM that halts all outgoing Ringg AI API requests immediately. Must be available to the Collections Manager without engineering intervention.

Health Alert: If the Ringg AI API returns failure codes for > 5% of leads in any rolling 1-hour window, an automated alert fires to the #tech-alerts Slack channel with failure rate, error codes, and timestamp.

Audit Trail: 100% of call recordings stored and retrievable via CRM. Collections Manager can filter by date, disposition, and loan ID.

14. Rollback Plan

If the bot's recovery rate falls below 15% over any 3-day window post go-live, or if a compliance violation is detected, the Kill Switch is activated and all bounce cases revert to the manual ELC queue. Engineering and Product are notified within 1 hour.

15. Pilot Summary & Baseline


16. Expected Benefits

Operational Efficiency: Reduces manual calling workload on bounce days by 50–70%.
Cost Optimization: Avoids hiring 3–4 additional collections agents at current scale.
Customer Experience: Instant outreach and real-time payment links in the Golden Window (7th–12th of each month). Scheduled reminders nudge customers at the exact moment they've committed to paying. Callback scheduling reduces repeat-call friction.
Scalability: Supports 1,500+ cases/month without proportional headcount increase.

17. Open Questions & Dependencies

Pincode Management

PRD | Version 1.0 | April 2026


1. Overview

This document defines the product requirements for an improved Pincode Management system within the GD CRM. The current implementation has functional gaps that create operational overhead for the product team, particularly when managing unserviceable pincodes for vendor configurations.

2. Background & Problem Statement

Vendors on the GD CRM are associated with a set of pincodes that determine where they can service education loan applications. Two separate systems currently govern this:

Serviceable pincodes are uploaded directly in the CRM.
Unserviceable pincodes must be separately updated in the BRE (Business Rules Engine).

Current Pain Points:

No visibility into what was previously uploaded — the uploaded sheet is not displayed anywhere against the vendor.
Dual-system overhead — product teams must manage serviceability status across CRM and BRE separately.
Performance degradation — when the unserviceable pincode list exceeds 100 entries, the BRE upload process slows significantly.
Full overwrites — any new file upload completely replaces existing pincode data, making incremental updates error-prone.

3. Goals & Non-Goals

Goals

Provide visibility into the currently active pincode sheet uploaded against each vendor.
Unify serviceable and unserviceable pincode management into a single upload workflow.
Implement incremental (merge-based) updates so new uploads amend existing data rather than overwriting it.
Reduce operational dependency on the BRE for routine pincode status changes.
Define a clear default state: vendors with no file uploaded are treated as serviceable across all pincodes.

Non-Goals

Real-time pincode lookups or API-based pincode eligibility checks.
Changes to the BRE's internal rules engine architecture.
Bulk deletion of pincodes (future release).

4. User Stories


5. Feature Requirements

5.1 Display Uploaded Pincode Sheet Against Vendor

Currently, after a pincode file is uploaded for a vendor, there is no way to view what was uploaded from within the portal.

Acceptance Criteria

The vendor detail page displays the filename and upload timestamp of the most recently uploaded pincode file.
A preview or download option is available so the user can inspect the current list.
If no file has been uploaded yet, the field displays: "No file uploaded — all pincodes serviceable"
The display updates immediately after a successful upload.

5.2 Upload File with Pincode + Serviceability Status

The upload format must be extended to include a status column alongside each pincode. This removes the need to separately update BRE for unserviceable pincodes.

File Format Specification


Acceptance Criteria

The system accepts CSV/XLSX uploads with columns: pincode and status.
status must be boolean true or false (case-insensitive). Rows with invalid values are rejected with a row-level error.
Pincodes with status = true are treated as serviceable.
Pincodes with status = false are treated as unserviceable (no separate BRE upload required).
A validation summary is shown post-upload: total rows processed, accepted, rejected (with reasons).

5.3 Default Serviceability When No File Is Uploaded

If no pincode file has ever been uploaded against a vendor, the system must treat that vendor as serviceable across all pincodes. Restrictions only come into effect once a file is explicitly uploaded and a specific pincode is marked false.

Acceptance Criteria

A vendor with no uploaded pincode file is considered serviceable for all pincodes.
No eligibility check should fail purely on pincode grounds for a vendor in this state.
Once a file is uploaded, only the pincodes present in the file (and their statuses) govern serviceability — the implicit "all serviceable" state no longer applies.
The vendor detail page clearly indicates "No file uploaded — all pincodes serviceable" when no file exists.

5.4 Incremental (Merge-Based) Upload Logic

New uploads must merge incoming data with what already exists — updating changed records, adding new ones, and leaving unmentioned pincodes untouched.

Merge Logic Rules


Acceptance Criteria

Uploading a file with an existing pincode updates only that pincode's status; all others remain unaffected.
Uploading a file with a new pincode appends it to the vendor's pincode list.
Pincodes absent from the new file are not modified or deleted.
The post-upload summary indicates: records updated / added / left unchanged / rejected.
If a pincode appears more than once in the same file, the last occurrence takes precedence and a warning is logged.

6. Functional Specification

6.1 Upload Flow (End-to-End)

User navigates to Vendor Configuration and selects a vendor.
User clicks "Upload Pincode File" and selects a CSV/XLSX with columns: pincode, status.
System validates the file format and each row's data. Invalid rows are flagged.
Valid rows are processed using merge logic (Section 5.4): existing pincodes updated, new ones inserted, unlisted ones untouched.
System displays an upload summary: rows updated, rows inserted, rows skipped (unchanged), rows rejected.
The vendor detail page reflects the new file reference and timestamp.

6.2 Error Handling


7. Out of Scope

Manual pincode entry via form (upload-only workflow for this release).
Pincode deletion — pincodes can only be updated to false, not removed.
Retroactive change history / audit log (future release).
Real-time BRE sync or webhook-based updates.

8. Dependencies & Assumptions

Dependencies

BRE team to confirm whether status=false pincodes via the new upload require any BRE-side configuration change.
Backend API to support merge-based upsert operation on the pincode table.
File storage service to retain the uploaded file for the display requirement (Section 5.1).

Assumptions

Each vendor has a single active pincode dataset at any point in time.
The authoritative pincode format is 6-digit numeric (standard Indian pincodes).
The status column accepts exactly two values: true and false (case-insensitive).
The merge operation is idempotent: uploading the same file twice produces the same result.
A vendor with no file uploaded is implicitly serviceable for all pincodes.

9. Open Questions


10. Success Metrics

Reduction in BRE upload events for unserviceable pincodes — target: 100% elimination post-launch.
Time taken to update pincode serviceability for a vendor reduces from multi-system workflow to a single upload.
Zero incidents of full-list overwrites causing unintended pincode loss after launch.
Upload error rate below 5% within 30 days of launch.

cards.title: Consultant Finder CRM Logic & Workflow Hardening
cards.body:
1. Problem Statement
The current Admissions CRM allows for "zombie leads" because next follow-up dates are not mandatory, leading to a lack of accountability for SSA. Furthermore, the CRM conflates "Commission Received" as a student stage, which obscures the student's actual progress in the application funnel once payment is made. This results in manual tracking for invoice raising and poor visibility into whether "Upfront Fee" students eventually convert to "Partner University" commissions. The current CRM tracks applications as a single linear path, which fails when a student applies to multiple universities. We lack a structured way to capture the shortlist at the point of application, and we cannot track which specific university has issued an offer versus those still pending. This leads to data gaps in our conversion funnel and manual follow-ups to "check" which offer the student is actually using. 
2. User Story
As an Admissions Lead, I want to enforce follow-up discipline and separate application stages from financial status so that we maximize student conversion and ensure 100% accuracy in revenue reporting for both upfront and partner commissions.I also want to track the status of every university application individually within a student’s profile so that I can accurately report on expected deposits
3. Acceptance Criteria (Executable Core)
AC 1: The Invoice Ledger (Child Table)
Given a SSA views the Stage dropdown, When they select a stage, Then "Commission Received" is no longer an option
Trigger: When Stage changes to "Upfront Fees Paid" or "Visa Done" by SSA.
UI Change: A child table Invoice Ledger becomes visible.
Workflow Step 1 (Admission Owner): * System sends an automated email to SSA Manager Role (currently: someone@example.com)
SSA Manager must add a row to the table and select Invoice Type (Partial Upfront, Complete Upfront, or University Commission).
Once saved, Invoice Status for that row defaults to "Started".
Workflow Step 2 (Finance Action): * Notification sent to Finance. Finance verifies: GrossAmount, Is Token? - NO, and Final Consultant.
Finance generates the invoice and must fill: Commission Amount (Mandatory) and Invoice Number.
Finance updates Invoice Status to "Invoice Generated".
Workflow Step 3 (Clearing):
When payment hits the bank, Finance updates status to "Cleared / Commission Received".
Logic for Multiple Invoices: If a student pays a partial fee (Row 1) and later pays the balance (Row 2), the system must allow adding a new row. 
Trigger: If Stage is set to "Upfront Fees Paid", the system must automatically check the Upfront Identifier checkbox and lock it with date (read-only).
AC 2: Mandatory Follow-up & Workday-Aware Guardrails
2.1 Mandatory Enforcement
Given any stage change (except "Paused"), When the user attempts to save, Then the Next Follow-up Date field is mandatory.
2.2 Workday-Only Validation
Logic: The system must validate the Next Follow-up Date against the Current Date using Business Days (excluding Sundays and dates uploaded in the Acme Holiday Master).
Validation Rule: The system must throw an error if the selected date exceeds the following Business Day (BD) limits:
Call Not Connected / NCY / Counselling Scheduled: +1 BD
GD Docs Awaited / Counselling Completed: +2 BD
Shortlisting Sent: +4 BD
Upfront Fees Paid / Consultant Awaiting Docs / Visa Done: +5 BD
Application Submitted / Some & All Offers Received: +10 BD
Visa Process Initiated: +15 BD
Paused / Consultant Pause: +90 Calendar Days (Holidays do not apply to Paused status).
2.3 Holiday & Weekend Blocks
Constraint: If the user selects a date that falls on a Sunday or a date present in the Holiday Master, the system must block the save and show: "Selected date is a non-working day. Please select the next available working day."
2.4 Business Owner Control (Holiday Master)
New UI: Create a simple Holiday Master table accessible only to the Business Owner.
Fields: Holiday Date, Occasion Name.
Upload: Provide a "Bulk Upload CSV" option for the Business Owner to upload the annual list of public holidays.
AC 3: The "Initial Deposit" Revenue Gate
GivenStage = "Initial Deposit Paid", Then the user must select the "Final University" from the list of universities previously entered in the Application Grid. 
Mandatory:University Type (Partner / Non-Partner) must be confirmed for this final choice. 
Action: Upon selecting "Initial Deposit Paid", the system must recheck the existing values for Country, University, Intake, and Course and force the user to re-select/re-save them to ensure data accuracy. Mandatory to choose Final Consultant
Field Requirement: If Stage = "Upfront Fees Paid", the following must be mandatory: Gross Amount, Is Token?, Remaining Installment, Expected Installment Date, and Final Consultant.
AC 4: Enrollment
New Stage: Create stage "Enrolled at University".
Trigger:When "Enrolled" is selected, the field Orientation Date becomes mandatory.
AC 5: The University Application Grid (New UI Component)
Trigger: When Stage is changed to "Application Submitted".
Behavior: A child table/grid must appear to capture the shortlist.
Fields per Row:University Name (Master Search), Course Name, Application Date, Application Status (Default: Submitted), University Type (Partner / Non-Partner)
Mandatory: At least one row must be filled to save the "Application Submitted" stage.


AC 6: Offer Tracking & Stage Renaming
Logic: * When in "Offer Letter Received", the user goes to the Application Grid and updates the Application Status for specific rows to Offer Received (Mandatory atleast one)
Mandatory Upload: For every row marked as Offer Received, an Offer Letter PDF upload field must appear and be filled.
Transition: The student cannot move to "Visa Process Initiated" unless at least one university in the grid has an Offer Received status AND a PDF uploaded.
4. Edge Cases
Manual Date Override: If a user tries to back-date a follow-up, the system must reject it.
Consultant Selection:Final Consultant must be a mandatory dropdown selection from the pre-approved master list of partners when "Upfront Fees Paid" or "Initial Deposit Paid" is selected.
The Grid Friction: Filling out a table for every university is more work for the CF. If you don't make the University/Course names a searchable "Master List," they will type "Harvard" five different ways, and your data reports will be useless.

cards.body:
Affected Area: /study-abroad/usa/ pages
Example Page
The Pittsburg State University PSU course page - is failing Google's Core Web Vitals (CWV) assessment on mobile devices.. The primary issues are:
Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): 2.5s (FAIL - target: ≤2.5s)
First Contentful Paint (FCP): 2.9s (FAIL - target: ≤1.8s)
Interaction to Next Paint (INP): 264ms (FAIL - target: ≤200ms)
Overall Performance Score: 42/100 (Critical)

Apart from this all the pages under /study-abroad/usa/ are getting deindexed from Google search results
The Problem
Your pages do not meet Google's Core Web Vitals thresholds on mobile. Google automatically removes pages that fail CWV from search rankings. This explains why your study-abroad pages have disappeared from mobile search results.
Key Metrics Breakdown

Root Causes
Based on PageSpeed Insights analysis, the main performance bottlenecks are:
Unoptimized Images (Est. savings: 283 KiB)
Images not compressed
Wrong formats (JPEG/PNG instead of WebP)
No lazy loading on below-the-fold images
Missing responsive image variants
Poor Cache Strategy (Est. savings: 207 KiB)
Static assets not cached properly
Missing cache headers (Cache-Control headers)
No CDN for global content delivery
Unused/Legacy JavaScript (Est. savings: 12 KiB)
Third-party scripts not optimized
Non-critical JS blocking render
No code splitting or lazy loading
Rendering Performance Issues
Forced reflow/repaint operations
Network dependency chain causing cascading delays
High Total Blocking Time (TBT: 1,480ms - should be <150ms)
Solution Plan (Priority Order)
Priority 1: Image Optimization (Est. 283 KiB savings)
What to do:
Convert all images to WebP format with PNG/JPEG fallbacks
Compress all images before upload using:
Squoosh (online)
TinyPNG (batch)
ImageOptim or similar desktop tool
Implement responsive images with srcset:
<img
src="image.webp"
srcset="image-mobile.webp 480w, image-tablet.webp 768w, image-desktop.webp 1200w"
alt="description"
width="800"
height="600"
/>
Add lazy loading to below-the-fold images:
<img src="image.webp" alt="description" loading="lazy" />
Always include explicit width/height to prevent layout shift
Expected Impact: Reduce FCP by ~0.5-0.8s
Priority 2: Browser Cache Optimization (Est. 207 KiB savings)
What to do:
Add cache headers to all static assets (CSS, JS, images, fonts)
Set HTTP cache-control headers:
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable (for versioned assets)
Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 (for HTML)
Implement service worker for offline caching
Use a CDN (Cloudflare, AWS CloudFront, Akamai) to serve all static content
Minify CSS and JavaScript
Expected Impact: Reduce repeat page loads by 40-60%
Priority 3: Remove Unused JavaScript (Est. 12 KiB savings)
What to do:
Audit all third-party scripts:
Google Analytics
Ads/ad networks
Tracking pixels
Font loading
Live chat widgets
Any other external JavaScript
Remove scripts that are not essential to the core page experience
Defer non-critical scripts using async or defer:
<script src="non-critical.js" async></script>
<script src="analytics.js" defer></script>
Implement code splitting so JS only loads when needed
Expected Impact: Reduce INP by ~50-80ms
Priority 4: Fix Forced Reflow & Rendering Issues
What to do:
Identify and eliminate forced reflow (batching DOM read/writes)
Move expensive computations out of the render path
Use CSS containment for complex layouts:
.container { contain: layout style paint; }
Minimize JavaScript execution time during page load
Split long-running tasks using requestIdleCallback()
Expected Impact: Reduce Total Blocking Time from 1,480ms to <300ms
Priority 5: Network Optimization
What to do:
Preload critical resources:
<link rel="preload" href="critical-font.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="preload" href="critical-image.webp" as="image">
Preconnect to third-party origins:
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://api.example.com">
DNS prefetch for non-critical third-party domains:
<link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://analytics.google.com">
Expected Impact: Reduce time to first byte (TTFB) by 100-200ms
Testing & Validation
Before making changes:
Take baseline screenshot from PageSpeed Insights
Document current Performance score (42/100)
After each fix:
Test locally using Lighthouse (Chrome DevTools → Audits)
Test on real mobile device (preferably Moto G or similar budget device)
Check performance on 4G throttled network
Final validation:
Run PageSpeed Insights on production URL
Verify all three metrics are in "PASS" zone:
LCP: ≤2.5s
FCP: ≤1.8s
INP: ≤200ms
Check that Performance score is ≥70
Re-submit URL to Google Search Console for reindexing
Monitor:
Set up continuous monitoring with PageSpeed Insights API or similar
Alert if metrics degrade in the future
Expected Outcomes
After implementing all fixes:
Performance Score: 42/100 → Target 75+/100
FCP: 2.9s → ~1.6-1.8s ✅
LCP: 2.5s → ~2.0-2.3s ✅
INP: 264ms → ~150-180ms ✅
Pages will be eligible for Google reindexing
Impact:
Restore mobile search visibility for all /study-abroad/usa/ pages
Improved user experience on mobile devices
Reduced bounce rate
Better Core Web Vitals score across all similar pages
Implementation Timeline
Day 1-2: Image optimization (highest impact)
Day 2-3: Cache implementation
Day 3: JavaScript cleanup
Day 4: Rendering fixes
Day 5: Testing & validation
Day 6: Google resubmission

cards.title: GD Scholarship Submit to GDC
NBFC Loan Closure: Foreclosure API + NOC Download in CRM
cards.body:
Problem

Loan closure today is a two-system workflow. The Ops user has to log into the external LMS, trigger foreclosure there, wait for the CRM status to sync, then go back to the LMS to download the NOC. This is slow (~5 min/closure), creates platform-switching overhead, and leaves the CRM as a passive observer rather than the system of action.

Objective

Make the CRM the single point of action for NBFC loan closure. The user initiates closure in the CRM, which calls the lender's Foreclosure API to update the external LMS, and then calls the NOC API to fetch and store the NOC directly inside the CRM — no LMS visit required.

Current Flow

Ops logs into external LMS → marks loan as closed
External LMS pushes status → CRM updates loan status
Ops returns to LMS → downloads NOC → uploads/shares manually

Proposed Flow

Ops opens loan in CRM → clicks Close Loan
CRM hits Foreclosure API → external LMS marks loan closed
On success, CRM hits NOC API → NOC PDF is fetched and attached to the loan record in CRM
Loan status auto-updates to Closed with NOC available for download from CRM itself

In Scope

"Close Loan" action on the loan detail page in CRM (with confirmation modal)
Foreclosure API integration with the NBFC (request + response handling, error states)
NOC API integration (fetch, store, display NOC against the loan)
Audit log: who triggered closure, timestamp, API response status
Failure handling: clear error messaging + retry option if either API call fails

Out of Scope

Bulk closure (single-loan only for v1)
Non-NBFC lenders (banks not on this foreclosure/NOC API stack)
Partial foreclosure / part-payment flows

Success Metrics

Time per closure: 5 min → 2–2.5 min (≥50% reduction)
Time saved: 250–300 min/month at current volume (100–125 closures/month)
% closures completed without LMS login: target ≥95%
API success rate: ≥98% for both Foreclosure and NOC calls

Dependencies / Open Questions

Confirm Foreclosure API and NOC API specs from the NBFC (auth, payload, response schema, sandbox availability)
Where should the NOC be stored — S3 / CRM document store? Naming convention?
Should NOC fetch be synchronous (block UI) or async (poll/webhook) if the lender takes time to generate it?
Permissioning: which roles can trigger closure?
Rollback / reversal: if NOC fetch fails after foreclosure succeeds, LMS-side closure is already done — retry-only flow, or do we need a manual override?

Engineering: TBD
Ops / ELC team: end users
NBFC partner: API owners

1. Problem Statement
When a Partnership Manager, Relationship Manager, or Team Lead  toggles a campaign partner's Cross-sell Whitelisting status to Yes or No within GD CRM, the underlying lead states don’t change downstream.
The Bandwidth Leak: Frappe CRM currently has no operational mechanism to ingest this upstream modification. Leads that were initially synced while Cross-sell Whitelisting = Yes remain active on sales floors even after the parameter is changed to No.
The Process Gap: Disbursement Executives continue calling, pitching, and following up with students whose partner channels have had their Cross-sell Whitelisting updated to No. This wastes  sales bandwidth and damages both customer and partner experiences.
2. User Story
As a Disbursement Executive, > I want Frappe CRM to instantly intercept incoming Cross-sell Whitelisting = No state updates from GD CRM and programmatically assign them to a newly created Ineligible status inside the Disbursement Status field,

So that these contacts are immediately removed from my active calling lists and manual follow-up queues, preventing me calling from not agreed partner leads.
3. Acceptance Criteria
AC 1: Core Schema Update & Dropdown Provisioning (Frappe Only)
Requirement: Modify the Disbursement Status dropdown field configuration inside the Student/Lead DocType. Append a new hardcoded operational sub-state:
Database Value / Label:Ineligible
Once a lead Disbursement status transitions to the Ineligible status state, then make it completely read-only and non-editable by the Disbursement Executive. 
AC 2: Real-Time Webhook Pipeline Setup
Trigger Event: The exact second a PM, RM, or SL updates a partner's profile settings in GD CRM that switches the core application parameters to Cross-sell Whitelisting = No.
Action: GD CRM must instantly fire an asynchronous PATCH request payload to the designated Frappe Lead.
AC 3: Conditional Interception & State-Lock Matrix (Frappe CRM Side)
Upon ingestion of the payload, Frappe CRM must perform an indexed lookup using the Mobile Number as the Primary Key. Before applying any database writes, the system must evaluate the current value of the local Disbursement Status field:
Rule 1: Permitted States for Opt-Out Transition
Condition: If the localized Disbursement Status inside Frappe is strictly equal to Follow-up OR CBCC.
System Action: Update the local Frappe Disbursement Status to Ineligible.
Queue Cleanup: Instantly strip the assignment from the active executive's workspace view, terminate any active follow-up tasks, and remove the record from all dialer or active callback queues.
Rule 2: Protected Revenue States (Immutable Rules)
Condition: If the localized Disbursement Status inside Frappe is already marked as Semi-Converted OR Converted.
System Action:DO NOT modify the status field. The local conversion pipeline takes complete data precedence to preserve active billing or won cycles.
4. Scope & Boundaries
In-Scope
Provisioning the Ineligible status variable inside Frappe configuration layers under the Disbursement Status option set.
Building the multi-state conditional routing script triggered during webhook ingestion mapping to the cross_sell_whitelisting parameter.
Out-of-Scope
Setting up reverse mechanics to turn the lead back on automatically if a partner's Cross-sell Whitelisting is set to Yes again later .
5. Technical Schema Requirements
Target Schema: Frappe DocType Lead / Student Master configuration fields.
Property Extension: Append the string type value "Ineligible" to the valid list values of the disbursement_status field property.
6. Success Metrics
Waste Reduction: Achieve a 100% elimination of redundant sales outreach calls made to students attached to partners whose Cross-sell Whitelisting is updated to No.

cards.body:
Question & Hypothesis
Question: With the payout module now LIVE for partners, which existing B2B Metabase queries need to be updated from "primary partner (LAS ranking=1)" logic to "payout eligible case" logic — and what is the downstream impact on B2C definitions?
Why now: The payout module is live. All B2B partner reporting currently identifies partner cases using loan_application_sources.ranking = 1 (primary partner attribution). The new payout module introduces a separate eligibility layer — a case may have a primary partner but NOT be payout-eligible (or vice versa). If we don't migrate, B2B numbers will diverge from what the partnership team sees in the payout module, and partner commission disputes will follow.
Hypotheses:
A significant number of B2B queries (dashboards, ad-hoc pulls, reports) use LAS ranking=1 + partner_type=0 as the B2B identifier — all of these need audit and potential migration.
B2C has historically been defined as "everything NOT in B2B" — if B2B scope changes (payout-eligible vs primary partner), B2C numbers will shift too. This needs stakeholder alignment before any query is rewritten.
Some queries may need BOTH views — historical (primary partner) and current (payout-eligible) — during the transition period.
Scope & Boundaries
In scope:
Audit ALL saved questions in the B2B Metabase collections (RM/PM Dashboard, ELC Dashboard, partner reports, ad-hoc pulls)
Document which queries use primary partner logic vs already use payout logic
Define the new B2B case identification rule (payout-eligible) with clear SQL pattern
Align with partnership team + finance on the new definition
Identify impact on B2C queries (anything that uses NOT IN B2B as its base)
Create a migration plan: which queries to update first, which need parallel views
Rewrite and test all affected queries
Out of scope:
Changes to the payout module itself (that's a tech/product card)
Historical data backfill (old cases won't retroactively become payout-eligible)
RBAC / access cleanup (separate card)
Methodology
Audit phase (Day 1-2):Pull the full list of saved questions in B2B Metabase collections
For each question, check if it references loan_application_sources.ranking = 1 with partner_type = 0 (current B2B logic)
Categorize: (a) needs migration, (b) already correct, (c) deprecated/junk (flag for RBAC card)
Document in a tracker sheet
Definition alignment (Day 3-4):Meet with partnership team stakeholders: What does "payout eligible" mean exactly? Which table/field/flag?
Meet with finance: How does payout eligibility affect commission reporting and invoice metrics?
Define the new SQL pattern for B2B identification (e.g., join to payout module table, check eligibility flag)
Define updated B2C = all leads NOT in new B2B scope
Document agreed definitions in a shared doc
Impact analysis (Day 4-5):Run both old (primary partner) and new (payout eligible) logic side by side for last 6 months
Quantify the gap: how many cases move in/out of B2B under the new definition?
Flag any queries where the gap is >5% — these need stakeholder sign-off before migration
Migration execution (Day 5-8):Update queries in priority order: live dashboards first, then recurring reports, then ad-hoc
Test each updated query against the old output — validate numbers with business team
Update B2C queries that depend on the B2B exclusion list
Handoff (Day 8):Share migration tracker with partnership team for validation
Document the new SQL patterns in the analytics knowledge base
Deliverable & Format
Migration tracker (Google Sheet): Every B2B Metabase query with status (migrated / pending / deprecated), old vs new logic, gap %
Definition doc (1-pager): Agreed B2B and B2C identification rules post-payout-module, with SQL examples
Updated Metabase queries: All B2B queries migrated and tested on prod
Audience: Partnership team (primary), Finance (secondary), Founders (for B2C impact awareness)
Timeline & Checkpoints


Decision Framework

cards.title: B2B Metabase RBAC cleanup — remove junk queries, structure data access for partnership team
cards.body:
Current State
The B2B Metabase space has accumulated queries over multiple sprints and ad-hoc requests without structured governance. Current problems:
Junk accumulation: Old, broken, or superseded queries sitting alongside live ones. Users don't know which queries to trust and which are stale.
No access structure: All B2B team members see all queries, including internal analytics, debug queries, and queries meant for specific roles (RM vs PM vs ELC vs SL).
No naming convention: Query names like "test_v2", "harsh_check", "final_final" mixed with production dashboards.
No ownership: When a query breaks or shows wrong numbers, it's unclear who owns it and whether it's still in use.
Risk: Business decisions being made on stale or incorrect queries because users can't distinguish live from deprecated.
Quantified pain: Unknown — part of this card is to audit and quantify how many queries exist, how many are actively used, and how many are junk. Estimate: 30-50% of saved questions in B2B collections are unused or superseded.
Target State
Clean collections: B2B Metabase organized into role-based collections:
B2B — RM/PM Dashboards (live dashboards for RM and PM users)
B2B — ELC Dashboards (live dashboards for ELC users)
B2B — Reports (recurring operational reports)
B2B — Internal / Analytics (debug, ad-hoc, WIP queries — visible to analytics team only)
B2B — Archived (deprecated queries kept for reference but hidden from business users)
RBAC applied: Each collection has appropriate permissions:
Partnership RMs/PMs: View access to RM/PM Dashboards + Reports only
ELCs/SLs: View access to ELC Dashboards + Reports only
Analytics team (Harsh, Gautam): Full access to all collections including Internal
Founders: View access to all collections
Naming convention enforced: [Live] RM/PM Performance Scorecard v6, [Report] Connectivity — RM/PM, [Archived] Old sanction tracker
Ownership documented: Each live query has an owner (who to ping when it breaks) in the query description
Technical Approach
Audit all B2B Metabase content (Day 1-2):Export full list of saved questions and dashboards in B2B collections
For each: record name, last run date, last edited date, creator, current collection
Classify: Live (actively used), Stale (not run in 30+ days), Junk (broken/superseded/test)
Share classification with Harsh for review
Stakeholder alignment (Day 2-3):Meet with partnership team leads: Which queries do you actually use? Which do you need?
Meet with ELC team leads: Same question
Identify gaps: queries they need but don't exist, vs queries that exist but nobody uses
Get explicit sign-off: "These N queries are junk, OK to archive"
Create collection structure (Day 3-4):Create the new collections in Metabase
Move live queries to appropriate role-based collections
Move junk/stale to Archived collection
Apply naming convention to all live queries
Add owner + description to each live query
Apply RBAC permissions (Day 4-5):Set up Metabase groups: B2B-RM-PM, B2B-ELC, Analytics-Internal
Map users to groups (get user list from partnership team)
Apply collection-level permissions: view/edit/none per group per collection
Test: log in as an RM user — confirm they see only what they should
Communicate and handoff (Day 5):Send Slack/email to B2B team: "Metabase has been reorganized — here's what changed"
Document the new structure and how to request new queries
Risks & Rollback


Rollback: Metabase collections can be reorganized in minutes. No queries are deleted — only moved to Archived. Permissions can be reverted by removing group restrictions.
Testing & Validation
Access test: Log in as each role (RM, PM, ELC, SL, analytics) and confirm correct visibility
No broken links: Verify all dashboard links in Slack/email still work (or redirects are set up)
Usage tracking: After 2 weeks, check Metabase audit log — are the right people using the right queries? Any "permission denied" errors?
Stakeholder confirmation: Partnership team lead confirms they can find everything they need
Timeline & Phases


Note: This card should ideally execute AFTER Card 1 (Payout module migration) — so the queries being organized are already on the new logic. If Card 1 is delayed, this card can still proceed but may need a second pass after migration.

cards.body:
Problem Statement

Currently, the WhatsApp message prompting users to share documents for loan verification is triggered directly from the Acme backend. This couples communication logic to application code, meaning any template change or messaging update requires a code deploy. Moving this trigger to MoEngage centralises all WhatsApp communications, allows non-dev template updates, and enables better analytics and audience control.

Affected users: All loan applicants who reach the document-submission step.

User Story

As a Acme operations/growth team member, I want the document-verification WhatsApp message to be triggered via MoEngage so that I can update the template, timing, and content without requiring an engineering deployment.

Scope & Boundaries

In scope:

Remove the backend WhatsApp API call that sends the document-verification message
Fire a MoEngage event at the same point in the flow to trigger the message
Switch WhatsApp template from Acme_doc_upload_request_v1 (old) to Acme_doc_upload_request_v2 (new)
QA in staging with test phone numbers before deploy

Out of scope:

Changes to any other WhatsApp templates or flows
Changes to SMS / email verification flows
MoEngage account setup or WhatsApp Business API configuration (assumed live)

WhatsApp Template Change


⚠️ Template Acme_doc_upload_request_v2 must be Meta-approved before go-live.

Acceptance Criteria

Given a user has completed the application step and document verification is pending,
When the trigger condition is met,
Then MoEngage fires a WhatsApp message using template Acme_doc_upload_request_v2 — and the backend does not fire the old API call.

Given MoEngage triggers the message,
When it is delivered,
Then message content matches the approved Acme_doc_upload_request_v2 template exactly.

Given MoEngage fails to deliver (event not received, opt-out, etc.),
When no message is sent,
Then the failure is logged and the fallback behaviour is documented (no silent drop).

Mid-migration duplicate sends — user already received v1 message; ensure MoEngage trigger de-dupes and doesn't resend.
MoEngage event attribute mismatch — if required user attributes (phone, opt-in status) are missing, define fallback / alerting.
WhatsApp opt-out discrepancy — user opted out in MoEngage but not in backend; MoEngage opt-out must be honoured and backend call must be gone.
Template not yet approved at deploy time — add a feature flag or deploy sequencing so old trigger isn't removed until new template is live.

MoEngage event name and user attribute mapping confirmed with MoEngage/tech team
Acme_doc_upload_request_v2 template approved by Meta
Backend code location of the existing WhatsApp API call identified and removed
Staging test run with real MoEngage events before production deploy

Success Metrics

100% of document-verification WhatsApp messages sent via MoEngage within 1 week of deploy
Zero duplicate messages during migration window
WhatsApp delivery rate ≥ baseline delivery rate of old templateProblem Statement
